tools.name: get_chart
tools.title: Read the chart
tools.description: Returns the chart spec (type, titles, axes, legend, series with ids and settings), its data as a table (header row of series names, then one row per category), grouped data as treeTable (path of names to each item, then its value) when the chart has a tree, the current selection, and a summary at the given size: per-series min / max / mean / trend, the axes as drawn, layout warnings (hidden labels, thinned lines), a colour check and a plain-language description. Use the series ids and category indexes it returns with the write tools.

tools.name: render_chart
tools.title: Render the chart
tools.description: Draws the chart without changing it so you can check how it looks: SVG text by default, or a PNG image with format "png" when the host can rasterize. Returns the layout warnings (hidden or thinned labels, dropped markers) alongside. An image costs tokens, so render after a batch of edits rather than after each one, and use it to check what text cannot tell you: overlapping or cut-off labels, a crowded legend, unreadable colours, whether the chart reads at the given size. For values, ids and warnings alone, get_chart is cheaper.

format.description: svg (default): the SVG document as text. png: an image to look at (only when the host can rasterize; costs image tokens).

time.description: Bar race only: the moment to draw (default: the one shown). Time point label (a category, e.g. "2023") or index from 0; an index may be fractional, 2.5 being halfway between the third and fourth time points.

tools.name: check_chart_colors
tools.title: Check chart colours
tools.description: Checks whether the chart's colours are accessible: that colour-blind readers can tell them apart (protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia, by OKLab distance after simulation) as well as people with normal vision, and that they stand out from the background. Checks the chart's own series (or slice) colours unless colours are given. Returns the closest pair per vision, contrast ratios and problems as sentences.

colors.description: Colours to check instead of the chart's (hex or rgb()).

tools.name: recommend_chart
tools.title: Recommend chart types
tools.description: Suggests chart types for data, best first, each with a reason: from CSV text when given, else from the chart's current data. Uses the shape of the data (series count, points, dates, negative values).

csv.description: CSV or TSV text to analyse instead of the current data (first row may be series names, first column categories).

tools.name: get_chart_trendline
tools.title: Read a trendline fit
tools.description: Returns a trendline's fitted coefficients (in x for category charts, x = 1, 2, 3, …), R², equation and the number of points, or the moving-average points.

series.description: Series id (from get_chart) or exact series name.

index.description: Trendline index on the series (0 = first).

tools.name: get_chart_tooltip
tools.title: Read a chart tooltip
tools.description: Returns what a viewer sees when hovering a category (or one series in it): the category label and, for each visible series with a value there, its name, colour, value, share (percent-stacked and pie charts, 0–1) and the value as the chart writes it. Returns null for charts without one value per category (histogram, box, treemap, sunburst, sankey, …) or when no visible series has a value there.

category.description: Category index (0-based) or exact category label.

series.description: Series id (from get_chart) or exact series name. Omit to include every visible series in the category.

tools.name: get_chart_race_ranking
tools.title: Read a bar race ranking
tools.description: Returns who leads a bar race at a moment without changing what is shown: the top raceTopN names with their rank, series id and value (eased between time points). Defaults to the moment shown. Works for any chart, reading categories as time points and series as names.

time.description: Time point label (a category, e.g. "2023") or index from 0; an index may be fractional, 2.5 being halfway between the third and fourth time points.

tools.name: list_chart_map_regions
tools.title: List map regions
tools.description: Lists the maps a choropleth can draw and the regions of one (default: the chart's map), each with the id and name that categories may use, and how the chart's categories match them: matched (category → region id) and unmatched. Use it to pick category labels before set_chart_data, and to fix unmatched ones.

tools.name: list_chart_presets
tools.title: List chart presets
tools.description: Lists the quick layouts and colour schemes apply_chart_preset accepts, with what each changes.

tools.name: export_chart_mermaid
tools.title: Export chart as Mermaid
tools.description: Returns the chart as Mermaid text for Markdown or chat: xychart-beta, pie or radar-beta, sankey-beta for Sankey diagrams with flows, treemap-beta for treemaps and sunbursts (with their levels). With meta (default true) one "%% @pixerate {…}" comment keeps what Mermaid cannot express, so import_chart_mermaid gets the chart back exactly.

tools.name: export_chart_ooxml
tools.title: Export chart as Office XML
tools.description: Returns the chart as a DrawingML chart part (c:chartSpace) for Word or PowerPoint files, with what could not be written as sentences.

tools.name: update_chart
tools.title: Change chart presentation
tools.description: Changes how the chart looks, as one undo step: type, titles, axes (xAxis = categories or numeric x, yAxis = values, yAxis2 = secondary values; each can be reversed, and value axes can be logarithmic with scale "log"), legend, stacking, orientation, curve, points, data labels and their position, palette, donut hole, bar spacing, histogram bins, waterfall total, radar rings (radarTicks) and grid shape (radarGraticule), note, highlight, reference lines and bands (whole lists), and varyColors. All-or-nothing: invalid values change nothing and come back as sentences. Returns the new spec.

type.description: Chart type. streamgraph stacks areas symmetrically around a center baseline; slope joins each category from the first series (before) to the second (after); likert reads each category as a question and the series as answers from most negative to most positive; parliament draws the first series as seats; sunburst draws the grouped data (set_chart_tree) as rings, and a treemap with grouped data nests its groups; sankey draws the flows (set_chart_links); barrace reads categories as time points and series as names, and animates their ranking; choropleth shades the regions of a map, each category naming a region by code (FRA) or name (France).

max.description: Fixed upper bound, or null for automatic.

step.description: Fixed distance between ticks, or null for automatic.

reverse.description: Run the axis the other way: values from the top down (or right to left), categories from the far end. Default false.

tools.name: import_chart_csv
tools.title: Import chart data from CSV
tools.description: Replaces the data with CSV or TSV text as one undo step. By default the first row holds series names and the first column categories (detected when "auto"). chartType "auto" also picks the recommended chart type (two unlabelled numeric columns become a scatter of x against y). Returns the data table, the chart type and cells that were not numbers.

csv.description: CSV or TSV text (tabs are detected).

seriesIn.description: Series run down columns (default) or along rows. Ignored with chartType "auto".

header.description: The first row holds series names: true (default), false or "auto". Ignored with chartType "auto".

chartType.description: "keep" (default) keeps the chart type; "auto" reads the table shape and picks a type.

tools.name: import_chart_mermaid
tools.title: Import a Mermaid chart
tools.description: Replaces the chart with Mermaid xychart-beta, pie, radar-beta, sankey-beta or treemap-beta text as one undo step (a "%% @pixerate" comment from export_chart_mermaid restores everything else). Lines that cannot be read are skipped and listed with their line numbers. Returns the spec.

mermaid.description: Mermaid text, optionally inside a ```mermaid fence.

backward.description: Extend the line this many x units before the first point (default 0).

intercept.description: Force the fit through this y at x = 0 (linear, polynomial, exponential).

showEquation.description: Write the fitted equation on the chart.

value.description: Where the line crosses its axis, in data units.

label.description: Text written on it, e.g. "Target" (default none).

axis.description: Axis it is measured on: y (default) is the value axis, y2 the secondary value axis (needs a series there), x the numeric x axis of a scatter or bubble chart.

tools.name: update_chart_reference_line
tools.title: Change a reference line
tools.description: Changes a reference line by index (all-or-nothing); label, axis and color take null to remove them. Returns the line as stored.

index.description: Reference line index (0 = first), as get_chart lists them in spec.referenceLines.

value.description: Where the line crosses its axis, in data units.

label.description: Text written on it; null removes it.

axis.description: Axis it is measured on (y, y2 or x); null goes back to y.

color.description: CSS colour; null goes back to the text colour.

tools.name: remove_chart_reference_line
tools.title: Delete a reference line
tools.description: Deletes a reference line by index; the ones after it move up one. Returns the reference lines left.

index.description: Reference line index (0 = first), as get_chart lists them in spec.referenceLines.

tools.name: add_chart_reference_band
tools.title: Add a reference band
tools.description: Shades a band across the plot between two values: a target or normal range (bar, line, area, scatter and bubble charts), drawn under the data. The axis grows to keep it in view. Returns its index and the reference bands.

from.description: One end of the band on its axis, in data units.

to.description: The other end of the band, in data units (ends may come in either order).

label.description: Text written on it, e.g. "Target" (default none).

axis.description: Axis it is measured on: y (default) is the value axis, y2 the secondary value axis (needs a series there), x the numeric x axis of a scatter or bubble chart.

tools.name: update_chart_reference_band
tools.title: Change a reference band
tools.description: Changes a reference band by index (all-or-nothing); label, axis and color take null to remove them. Returns the band as stored.

index.description: Reference band index (0 = first), as get_chart lists them in spec.referenceBands.

from.description: One end of the band on its axis, in data units.

to.description: The other end of the band, in data units (ends may come in either order).

label.description: Text written on it; null removes it.

axis.description: Axis it is measured on (y, y2 or x); null goes back to y.

color.description: CSS colour; null goes back to the text colour.

tools.name: remove_chart_reference_band
tools.title: Delete a reference band
tools.description: Deletes a reference band by index; the ones after it move up one. Returns the reference bands left.

index.description: Reference band index (0 = first), as get_chart lists them in spec.referenceBands.

tools.name: set_chart_callout
tools.title: Pin a label to a point
tools.description: Pins a short label to one bar or point, with a leader line, to say why it matters ("Record quarter", "Launch"); label null or "" removes it. Bar, line, area, scatter and bubble charts; the point must have a value. Selects the point and returns the series id, category index and label.

series.description: Series id (from get_chart) or exact series name.

category.description: Category index (0-based) or exact category label.

label.description: The label (keep it to a few words), or null to remove it.

annotations.title: Pin a label to a point

tools.name: highlight_chart
tools.title: Highlight categories or series
tools.description: Draws the named categories (labels) and series (names or ids) normally and mutes the rest, to draw attention to the marks the chart is about; [] shows everything again. A point stays bright when its category or its series is named. Unknown names change nothing and are reported. Returns the category indexes and series ids that matched.

names.description: Category labels and / or series names or ids, exactly as get_chart shows them. [] clears the highlight.

tools.name: set_chart_tree
tools.title: Replace grouped data
tools.description: Replaces the chart's data with groups of items (a tree) for treemaps and sunbursts, as one undo step: items {"name", "value"} and groups {"name", "children"}, up to 6 levels, names unique among siblings. The top-level groups become the categories and their totals the first series, so other chart types draw the totals. [] goes back to plain data (the totals stay as values). Returns the tree, each group's total and the depth.

tree.description: The top-level nodes; [] removes the grouping.

chartTreeNode.description: An item ({"name", "value"}) or a group ({"name", "children": [nodes]}, whose value is the sum of its items).

value.description: Items only: the amount, 0 or more.

children.description: Groups only: the nodes inside it (up to 6 levels in all).

color.description: CSS colour (default: the palette colour of its top-level group, lighter further in).

tools.name: import_chart_tree_csv
tools.title: Import grouped data from CSV
tools.description: Replaces the data with grouped data from CSV or TSV: every column but the last holds names (group, subgroup, …, item), the last holds the value. A blank group name repeats the one above, as spreadsheets lay out groups. One undo step. Returns the tree, group totals and depth.

header.description: The first row holds column names (default auto: when its last cell is not a number).

tools.name: add_chart_tree_node
tools.title: Add an item or group
tools.description: Adds an item or a group (with children) under a group of the grouped data, or at the top level. Returns its path and its parent's new total.

parent.description: Path of the group to add to; [] or omitted for the top level.

node.description: The item ({"name", "value"}) or group ({"name", "children"}) to add.

at.description: Position among its siblings (default: the end).

chartTreeNode.description: An item ({"name", "value"}) or a group ({"name", "children": [nodes]}, whose value is the sum of its items).

value.description: Items only: the amount, 0 or more.

children.description: Groups only: the nodes inside it (up to 6 levels in all).

color.description: CSS colour (default: the palette colour of its top-level group, lighter further in).

tools.name: update_chart_tree_node
tools.title: Change an item or group
tools.description: Renames a node, sets an item's value, or sets a node's colour (null goes back to the palette). Groups have no value of their own. Returns the node's path (new if renamed) and the node.

path.description: Names from the top level down to the node, e.g. ["Europe", "France"] (from get_chart treeTable or spec.tree).

color.description: CSS colour, or null for the palette colour.

tools.name: remove_chart_tree_node
tools.title: Delete an item or group
tools.description: Deletes a node of the grouped data with everything under it (a group left empty becomes an item with value 0). Returns the group totals left.

path.description: Names from the top level down to the node, e.g. ["Europe", "France"] (from get_chart treeTable or spec.tree).

tools.name: set_chart_links
tools.title: Replace the flows
tools.description: Replaces the chart's data with flows between named nodes for a Sankey diagram, as one undo step: each {"source", "target", "value"} with a value above 0. Flows only go forwards (no loops) and a source-target pair appears once. The nodes become the categories and how much passes through each the first series. nodes (optional) sets the stacking order. [] goes back to plain data. Returns the flows and each node's throughput.

source.description: Name of the node the flow leaves.

target.description: Name of the node it reaches (a different node; flows only go forwards, no loops).

nodes.description: Node names in stacking order (default: as the flows first name them).

tools.name: import_chart_links_csv
tools.title: Import flows from CSV
tools.description: Replaces the data with flows from CSV or TSV rows of source, target and value (as Mermaid sankey-beta and spreadsheets write them). One undo step. Returns the flows and each node's throughput.

header.description: The first row holds column names (default auto: when its third cell is not a number).

tools.name: add_chart_link
tools.title: Add a flow
tools.description: Adds a flow from one node to another (new names add nodes). Refused when the pair exists already or it would close a loop. Returns its index and the throughput of its two nodes.

source.description: Name of the node the flow leaves.

target.description: Name of the node it reaches (a different node; flows only go forwards, no loops).

tools.name: update_chart_link
tools.title: Change a flow
tools.description: Changes a flow by index: its source, target, value or colour (null goes back to the default). Checked like a new flow. Returns the flow as stored.

index.description: Flow index (0 = first), as get_chart lists them in spec.links.

source.description: Name of the node the flow leaves.

target.description: Name of the node it reaches (a different node; flows only go forwards, no loops).

color.description: CSS colour, or null for the default.

tools.name: remove_chart_link
tools.title: Delete a flow
tools.description: Deletes a flow by index; the ones after it move up one, and nodes no flow uses any more go. Returns the flows left.

index.description: Flow index (0 = first), as get_chart lists them in spec.links.

tools.name: set_chart_race_frame
tools.title: Show a bar race moment
tools.description: Shows the bar race at a time point (or between two), and stops playback. This is view state like the selection: it is not an undo step and is not saved in the chart. Returns the moment and the ranking shown.

time.description: Time point label (a category, e.g. "2023") or index from 0; an index may be fractional, 2.5 being halfway between the third and fourth time points. null shows the last time point.

tools.name: play_chart_race
tools.title: Play the bar race
tools.description: Starts playing the bar race for the user from the moment shown (from the start when it is at the end), one time point every msPerStep ms, and returns at once. set_chart_race_frame stops it. Nothing in the chart changes.

tools.name: apply_chart_preset
tools.title: Apply a chart style
tools.description: Applies a quick layout (legend, labels and grid lines together) and / or a colour scheme as one undo step. See list_chart_presets for the names. Returns the new spec.

tools.name: transpose_chart
tools.title: Switch rows and columns
tools.description: Swaps series and categories (each category becomes a series) as one undo step. Per-series colours and settings are dropped. Returns the data table.

tools.name: select_chart_element
tools.title: Select a chart element
tools.description: Selects part of the chart (as a click would), for press_chart_key and for the user to see. kind "none" clears the selection. Returns the selection.

series.description: Series id or name (series, point, trendline).

tools.name: drag_chart_point
tools.title: Drag a chart point
tools.description: Drags on the chart as a pointer would, through the same code as the mouse: from a bar or point to a new position, with the same snapping (to other values, zero and ticks), fine adjustment (fine: Alt) and axis lock on scatter charts (lockAxis: Shift). Positions are 0–1 fractions of the chart's width and height at the given size (use render_chart to see where marks are). One undo step. Returns what was dragged and the value before and after.

from.description: Start, as fractions of the chart (0,0 top-left).

to.description: End, as fractions of the chart.

lockAxis.description: Scatter charts: change only the axis moved along most (Shift).

tools.name: press_chart_key
tools.title: Press a key on the chart
tools.description: Sends a key to the chart as the keyboard would, acting on the selection (select_chart_element first): ← → move between categories, ↑ ↓ change the selected value by a tenth of a tick (shift: a whole tick, alt: a hundredth), Delete removes the selection, Escape clears it. Returns whether the key did anything and the new selection.

annotations.title: Press a key on the chart

tools.name: undo_chart
tools.title: Undo a chart edit
tools.description: Undoes the last chart edit. Returns whether something was undone and what the next undo would be.

tools.name: redo_chart
tools.title: Redo a chart edit
tools.description: Redoes the last undone chart edit. Returns whether something was redone.

tools.name: check_chart_style
tools.title: Check chart house style
tools.description: Checks the chart against the house style (see get_style with domain "chart"): runs the checks its profile turns on (palette-only, distinguishable, min-contrast, allowed-type). Returns findings with a severity, a sentence saying how to fix it, a target selection (series id or point) for update_chart_series or update_chart, and the layer that asked for it; plus the checks that ran and the ones skipped with the reason. Check after a batch of edits and again after fixing.

tools.name: apply_chart_style
tools.title: Apply the chart house style
tools.description: Starts the chart from the house style, as one undo step: sets the house palette and the spec defaults the style names (data labels, curve, stacking, orientation, label position). Use it on a new chart or when the user asks to bring a chart in line; it does not touch data, titles or series colours set by hand (check_chart_style reports those). Returns the patch applied and the new spec. Fails, changing nothing, when no house style applies to charts or the chart is read-only.

tools.name: list_open_files
tools.title: List open files
tools.description: Lists the Office files the user opened that charts can be read from. Returns their names and sizes in bytes.

tools.name: list_file_charts
tools.title: List the charts in an Office file
tools.description: Reads an Excel workbook, PowerPoint deck or Word document and lists its charts in file order: id, where it sits (sheet name and anchor cell, or slide number), title, type, series names, number of categories, read problems, features the chart editor cannot hold, and whether it reads losslessly. Pass an id to get_file_chart or load_file_chart.

file.description: Name of an open file, as list_open_files returns it.

annotations.title: List the charts in an Office file

tools.name: get_file_chart
tools.title: Get a chart from an Office file
tools.description: Returns one chart of an Office file with its full chart spec (data, axes, series styles), where it sits and its read problems.

file.description: Name of an open file, as list_open_files returns it.

annotations.title: Get a chart from an Office file

tools.name: load_file_chart
tools.title: Load a chart from an Office file
tools.description: Replaces the chart in the editor with a chart from an Office file, as one undo step. Returns the new spec, read problems and features the editor could not keep.

file.description: Name of an open file, as list_open_files returns it.

annotations.title: Load a chart from an Office file
